q: A 1,800 sq ft dwelling has two small-appliance circuits, one laundry circuit, a 12 kW range and a 5 kW dryer. Using the standard method, the total calculated load is approximately:
explain: Lighting 1,800 × 3 = 5,400 + 4,500 (SA + laundry) = 9,900 VA → 3,000 + 0.35 × 6,900 = 5,415 VA. Range 8,000 VA (Table 220.55 Col. C). Dryer 5,000 VA. Total 18,415 VA ÷ 240 V ≈ 77 A — so the 100 A minimum of 230.79(C) governs.

q: The demand load for one 15 kW household range is:
explain: Column C gives 8 kW for up to 12 kW. For each kW over 12, add 5%: 3 kW over → 15% → 8 × 1.15 = 9.2 kW.

q: A four-unit building has one 5 kW electric dryer per unit. The dryer demand load for the service is:
explain: Table 220.54 applies 100% for 1–4 dryers: 4 × 5 kW = 20 kW. Demand factors begin at 5 dryers (85%).

q: Under the dwelling optional method, central electric space heating (including a heat pump's supplemental heat) is included at what percentage of nameplate?
explain: 220.82(C): air conditioning 100%; central electric space heating 65%; fewer than four separately controlled heating units 65%; four or more separately controlled units 40%. Use only the largest of the heating/cooling options.

q: An office has 100 general-use receptacle outlets (180 VA each). Applying Table 220.44, the receptacle demand load is:
Using the 83% rule, the minimum copper conductor for a 150 A one-family dwelling service is:
explain: 150 × 0.83 = 124.5 A → 1 AWG Cu (130 A at 75°C). Table 310.12 lists 1 AWG Cu / 2/0 Al for 150 A.

q: A service has 3/0 AWG copper service-entrance conductors. The minimum copper grounding electrode conductor to a metal water pipe electrode is:
explain: Table 250.66: 2/0 or 3/0 copper → 4 AWG copper GEC. (The 6 AWG cap applies only to the portion that is the sole connection to a rod, pipe or plate.)

q: A 60 A branch circuit requires a copper equipment grounding conductor of at least:
explain: Table 250.122: 30, 40 and 60 A → 10 AWG copper. 100 A → 8 AWG.

q: A 20 A circuit's 12 AWG ungrounded conductors (6,530 cmil) are upsized to 8 AWG (16,510 cmil) for voltage drop. The equipment grounding conductor must be increased to at least:
explain: Ratio = 16,510 / 6,530 ≈ 2.53. Required EGC = 6,530 × 2.53 ≈ 16,500 cmil → 8 AWG. Wire-type EGCs are upsized in proportion to the circular-mil increase.

q: A 25-ft tap is made from a feeder protected at 400 A. The minimum copper tap conductor (75°C) is:
explain: Tap ampacity ≥ 1/3 × 400 = 133.3 A. 1 AWG (130 A) falls short; 1/0 AWG (150 A) is the first size that qualifies.

q: A branch circuit supplies 80 A of continuous lighting load. The equipment is rated for 75°C terminations. Minimum copper conductor size?
explain: 80 × 1.25 = 100 A minimum ampacity before adjustment → 3 AWG Cu at 75°C (100 A). OCPD likewise 100 A (210.20(A)).

q: A service's calculated neutral load is 300 A. Applying the neutral demand factor, the required neutral ampacity is:
explain: The portion of the unbalanced load over 200 A may be reduced 30%: 200 + 0.7 × 100 = 270 A. Not permitted for the nonlinear-load portion.

q: Under the 2020 Code, a kitchen island with 36 sq ft of countertop requires at least how many receptacle outlets?
explain: One receptacle for the first 9 sq ft, plus one for each additional 18 sq ft or fraction: 36 − 9 = 27 → 27 / 18 = 1.5 → 2 more. Total 3.

q: A dwelling bathroom receptacle must be located within how far of the outside edge of each basin?
explain: Within 3 ft of the outside edge of the basin, on a wall or partition adjacent to it, or on the side/face of the cabinet (not more than 12 in. below the countertop).

q: An attached garage with electric power requires at least one branch circuit that is:
choices: 20 A, 120 V, serving garage receptacles with no other outlets (readily accessible outdoor receptacles excepted)
Any rating, shared with the laundry
explain: A dedicated 120 V, 20 A circuit for garage receptacle outlets; it may also supply readily accessible outdoor receptacles.

q: Overhead service conductors (300 V or less) pass over a roof with a slope of at least 4 in 12. The minimum clearance above the roof may be reduced to:
explain: General rule is 8 ft above the roof; 3 ft is permitted for roofs sloped 4 in 12 or steeper when voltage does not exceed 300 V between conductors.

q: The system bonding jumper for a separately derived system (such as a transformer secondary) is sized according to:
choices: Table 250.102(C)(1) using the derived phase conductors
explain: Same table as the service main bonding jumper, based on the derived (secondary) ungrounded conductors. The SDS grounding electrode conductor is sized from Table 250.66.

q: A metal in-ground support structure (building steel) qualifies as a grounding electrode when it is in direct contact with the earth vertically for at least:
explain: 10 ft or more, with or without concrete encasement. Multiple structures bonded together count as one electrode.

q: At an existing building, a concrete-encased electrode is NOT required to be part of the grounding electrode system when:
choices: The building has a metal water pipe
Using it would require disturbing the concrete
A ground rod is driven instead
explain: The exception covers existing buildings where the rebar is not accessible without disturbing the concrete. New construction must use the Ufer when present.

q: A 100 A feeder carries the entire load of a one-family dwelling to its main panel. Using Table 310.12, the minimum copper feeder conductor is:
explain: The 83% table applies to the main power feeder as well as the service: 100 A → 4 AWG Cu (2 AWG Al).

q: A multifamily service supplies 12 ranges, each rated 12 kW. Using Column C, the range demand load is:
explain: Column C, 12 appliances → 27 kW. (Column C runs 8 kW for one range up to 15 kW + 1 kW per range above 30.)

q: A dwelling's standard-method calculated load is 18,415 VA at 240 V (≈ 77 A). The minimum service disconnect rating and the minimum copper service conductor (Table 310.12) are:
explain: 230.79(C) sets 100 A as the floor for a one-family dwelling regardless of the 77 A calculation; Table 310.12 gives 4 AWG Cu for 100 A.
